'''Herman Frederik Nijhout''' (born November 25, 1947)<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n90714160.html |title=Nijhout, H. Frederik |website=Library of Congress Name Authority File |access-date=2018-12-20}}</ref> is a Dutch-born American evolutionary biologist and the [[John Franklin Crowell]] Professor of Biology at [[Duke University]]. His research is focused on [[evolutionary developmental biology]] and [[entomology]], with a particular focus on the hormonal control of growth, molting and metamorphosis in [[insects]], including the mechanisms that control the development of alternative phenotypes.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://sites.biology.duke.edu/nijhout/ |title=Fred Nijhout's Lab Page |website=Duke University |access-date=2018-12-20}}</ref> Much of his work has also been concerned with understanding the development and evolution of the wing patterns of  [[butterflies]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1994/07/05/science/how-nature-makes-a-butterfly-s-wing.html |title=How Nature Makes a Butterfly's Wing |last=Wade |first=Nicholas |date=1994-07-05 |work=The New York Times |access-date=2018-12-20 |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>  He received the ESA Founders' Memorial Award from the [[Entomological Society of America]] in 2006.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://biology.duke.edu/people/h-frederik-nijhout |title=H. Frederik Nijhout |website=Duke University |access-date=2018-12-20}}</ref> In 2015, he was awarded the [[A.O. Kowalevsky Medal]], and in 2018, he was elected a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2018/04/four-professors-elected-as-2018-american-academy-of-arts-and-sciences-fellows |title=Four professors elected as 2018 American Academy of Arts and Sciences fellows |last=Vashisth |first=Shagun  |date=2018-04-18 |work=Duke Chronicle |access-date=2018-12-20}}</ref> He was elected a Member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2025.<ref>https://www.nasonline.org/news/2025-nas-election/</ref>
